title: Surviving the 14-day lunar night
bottleneck: The lunar day-night cycle lasts about 29.5 Earth days, so a Moon base endures 14 straight days of darkness at -173 C with no solar power. Batteries at the required scale would weigh hundreds of tons; regenerative fuel cells lose energy in the round trip; beaming power from orbit or sunlit crater rims works only near the poles. Fission power solves it but brings its own unsolved deployment challenges. Every non-nuclear architecture must carry two weeks of energy storage — a mass penalty dominating base design.
why_it_blocks: Power is survival — heat, air, and water recycling all stop without it; the lunar night is the single largest sizing driver for any Moon base power system.
current_state: NASA studies favor fission surface power for this reason; battery and fuel-cell options exist only for short sorties. No base-scale night-survival power system has been built or tested.
